Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE six-frame NORTH RUN animation sprite sheet for the Caatuu macaw traveler, 1536 by 1024 landscape. Exactly 3 columns by 2 rows, ALL SIX CELLS OCCUPIED, chronological order left-to-right then top-to-bottom. This is a new run cycle, not a reproduction of the five-pose walking layout in the reference.
Reference Image 1: the accepted NORTH walking sheet is ONLY the character identity, costume, rear direction and pixel-style authority. Preserve this exact round blue macaw, blue feather hands and short central blue tail, brown robe with golden collar/cuffs/hem, hood down, centered brown travel backpack with two gold buckles and small front pocket. Preserve proportions, pixel density, colors, outline weight and gently elevated RPG camera. No hat. Show only back/top of blue head in every cell: no eyes, facial patches or beak. Face directly AWAY toward screen top throughout, never turn sideways.
Composition: six complete isolated full-body sprites, each at the SAME scale, evenly centered within six equal 512x512 cells. Leave at least 40 pixels of clear gutter from every silhouette to each cell boundary. No overlap, no cropping, no drawn grid, labels or numbers. Medium-detail pixel art, same sharp square pixel clusters as the reference, no painting or smoothing.
Movement: energetic RUN toward screen top, with a modest forward lean AWAY from camera, a clear grounded compression and two airborne phases. Only two anatomically attached bird legs and two blue feather arms. Golden toes/claws point logically with the movement, not reversed flippers. Modest robe and backpack sway and body bounce, constant head/backpack/body sizes.
IMPORTANT ARM CONTRAST: the first and second half of the run MUST reverse the arm swing. In this direct BACK view, anatomical LEFT is viewer LEFT. A forward arm swings AWAY from camera, bends at the elbow and sits higher beside the robe; a backward arm swings TOWARD camera and is more visible/lower. Keep both attached to shoulders; do not hide or duplicate them. Feet alternate support.
Exact six chronological poses:
CELL 1 top-left: LEFT foot contacts forward AWAY, higher under the hem; RIGHT leg trails toward viewer, foot lower. LEFT arm BACK toward viewer, RIGHT arm FORWARD away. One foot supports.
CELL 2 top-middle: LEFT leg supports with knee/body compressed; RIGHT knee drives forward under the body. Arms pass through neutral beside the torso. Both arms readable. This is the first support moment.
CELL 3 top-right: AIRBORNE after left push-off, RIGHT leg reaches forward AWAY, LEFT leg trails toward viewer and bends upward. BOTH feet off ground. LEFT arm FORWARD away, RIGHT arm BACK toward viewer. Body a little higher than support poses, not resized.
CELL 4 bottom-left: RIGHT foot contacts forward AWAY, LEFT leg trails toward viewer. LEFT arm FORWARD away, RIGHT arm BACK toward viewer. This is the exact opposite limb-role contact to cell 1.
CELL 5 bottom-middle: RIGHT leg supports with knee/body compressed; LEFT knee drives forward under the body. Arms pass through neutral, opposite leg support from cell 2. No standing duplicate.
CELL 6 bottom-right: AIRBORNE after right push-off, LEFT leg reaches forward AWAY, RIGHT leg trails toward viewer and bends upward. BOTH feet off ground. LEFT arm BACK toward viewer, RIGHT arm FORWARD away. Opposite limb roles from cell 3, ready to loop into cell 1.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha preferred. If alpha is unavailable use plain pure white, with no checkerboard pixels, glow, cast shadow or ground. No scenery, staff, magic, extra props, captions or watermark.
Deliver one complete six-pose sheet. The final bottom-right cell is a real sixth running pose, NOT EMPTY.

Reference image is ONLY the approved character identity, south camera, costume, proportions and medium-detail pixel style. The reference contains walking poses; replace those with the six running poses specified here. Draw all six together so face, beak, head size and costume details remain consistent.

Canvas: LANDSCAPE 1536 x 1024, invisible grid of THREE equal columns and TWO equal rows. Exactly SIX complete macaws, one per cell; all six cells occupied. Chronological order left to right across top row (1,2,3), then left to right bottom row (4,5,6). Each full figure fits in its 512x512 cell, about390px tall, with at least40px clear margins/gutters, no overlap or clipped hands/feet. Match head size and body anchor within every cell. NO drawn grid, labels, numbers, captions or diagram arrows.

Every character faces SOUTH directly toward viewer, both cream cheek patches and both eyes visible, at the same slightly elevated RPG camera. Rounded teal-blue head, centered ochre hooked beak with dark lower beak, friendly dark eyes; brown travel wizard robe with gold trim and hood DOWN, brown belt with brass buckle, two brown backpack straps with brass fasteners, blue feather hands, short blue legs, gold bird feet with natural dark claws. No hat, staff or added accessory. Keep the exact reference identity and refined pixel clusters; do not enlarge head, lengthen legs, change palette or redesign the outfit. A modest lean toward the viewer conveys forward running, with lively but controlled robe and hand movement.

ANATOMICAL LEFT IS SCREEN RIGHT. ANATOMICAL RIGHT IS SCREEN LEFT.
Six chronological RUN poses:
1 TOP LEFT: LEFT-forward CONTACT. Screen-RIGHT blue leg reaches toward viewer, its gold foot is lower/closer and touches down. Screen-LEFT leg trails higher behind. LEFT arm on screen right swings BACK, RIGHT arm on screen left swings FORWARD (bent elbow, larger visible fist toward viewer). Keep hands clear of torso.
2 TOP MIDDLE: LEFT SUPPORT/COMPRESSION. Screen-right leg supports beneath body with bent knee; body dips slightly. Screen-left knee lifts and swings forward under the hem. Both elbows pass nearer neutral as they exchange direction. This is a compact running support, not idle.
3 TOP RIGHT: FLIGHT after LEFT push-off. BOTH feet lifted clear of ground. LEFT/screen-right leg trails back, bent and tucked high; RIGHT/screen-left leg reaches forward toward viewer, its foot lower/closer. LEFT arm on screen RIGHT swings FORWARD visibly; RIGHT arm on screen left swings BACK. This arm arrangement is opposite pose1.
4 BOTTOM LEFT: RIGHT-forward CONTACT. Screen-LEFT gold foot touches down low toward viewer; screen-RIGHT leg trails higher behind. LEFT arm on screen RIGHT swings FORWARD, RIGHT arm on screen LEFT swings BACK. This is the opposite contact stride to pose1.
5 BOTTOM MIDDLE: RIGHT SUPPORT/COMPRESSION. Screen-left leg supports beneath body with bent knee; screen-right knee lifts forward under the hem. Body slightly compressed, arms pass near neutral. Opposite support to pose2.
6 BOTTOM RIGHT: FLIGHT after RIGHT push-off. BOTH feet lifted. RIGHT/screen-left leg trails bent and tucked high; LEFT/screen-right leg reaches forward toward viewer, its foot lower/closer. LEFT arm on SCREEN RIGHT swings BACK; RIGHT arm on SCREEN LEFT swings FORWARD. This must be visibly OPPOSITE to pose3 and naturally lead back into pose1.

Contact and flight poses have clear alternating legs and opposing arm swings. Two anatomically attached legs and two attached ankles per macaw, natural bird toes oriented toward travel. No duplicated limb, detached foot, sideways step, repeated idle, marching or symmetric hopping. Flight3 and6 are suspended above an imaginary common ground line; no ground is drawn. Keep head/costume rigidly consistent, only restrained running bob and cloth movement. Preserve reference's medium-detail crisp pixel clusters and warm dark outline; not coarse low-resolution art and not smooth painting.

Background: genuinely transparent alpha if possible. Otherwise completely uniform SOLID WHITE is fine. NEVER paint a checkerboard, gradient, glow, ground shadow, floor or scenery. Exactly six fullbody run sprites, nothing else.

phase_qa.observation: Screen-right foot forward/low, screen-left hand forward. Correct opposite limb arrangement.

Screen-left leg reaches forward, screen-right leg trails tucked. Screen-right hand forward, opposite phase 1. Both feet visibly lifted relative to contact baseline.
Screen-left foot forward/low and screen-right hand forward, correctly opposite phase 1.
Screen-left support foot lower, screen-right knee raised. Correct opposite support from phase 2.
Screen-right leg forward, screen-left leg trails; screen-left hand forward, correctly opposite phase 3. Both feet visibly lifted relative to contact baseline.
